world 0 (key overran).reader_note: Miners camped in the churchyard until the council stopped meeting; the final sentence (same families, same fields, street still facing the landing) explicitly kills ruined, reoriented and repopulated.

world 1 (key repopulated).reader_note: D 'overran' is struck on grammar alone: 'had overran' is not English (needs the participle 'overrun'). 400 to 1,900 nearly hands over repopulated; 'main street still facing the river landing' kills reoriented.

world 2 (key ruined).reader_note: 'overran' is ungrammatical after 'had' (needs 'overrun'), so D falls on grammar alone; population halved kills repopulated and 'main street still facing the river landing' kills reoriented.

world 3 (key reoriented).reader_note: Trade moving from the river landing to the back street with the population steady at about eight hundred decides reoriented; the steady population kills repopulated and ruined, and nothing supports overran.

world 1 (key pitted).reader_note: Scattered open pits with forest between gives pitted; 'dug out from above' kills riddled (tunnels), the cairn and forest kill razed, trout kill poisoned.

world 2 (key razed).reader_note: Taken from above bench by bench, summit four hundred feet lower, decides razed; no tunnels kills riddled, flat shelf kills pitted, rising trout kill poisoned.

world 3 (key poisoned).reader_note: 'a single shaft from one deep vein' kills riddled, slopes and cairn looking as in old photographs kill razed and pitted; orange water, vanished trout and dead streamside forest give poisoned.

world 0 (key riddled).reader_note: Each distractor is killed by one planted phrase: razed and pitted by 'look as they do in old photographs', poisoned by 'trout still rise'; riddled follows from the subsidence (road dropping, spring vanishing, floors splitting).

world 3 (key padlocked).reader_note: 'Every book stood in its place... the catalog matched the shelves card for card' kills plundered, pulped and purged on a surface read; all three destructive P-words fail together, leaving the only non-destructive option.

world 0 (key plundered).reader_note: Rare books gone, ordinary left, stamped volumes surfacing in the occupier's universities decide plundered; purged needs an ideological removal never mentioned, pulped is killed by the books turning up.

world 1 (key purged).reader_note: 'every book by some two hundred writers, most of them critics of the occupiers, had gone, along with those writers' catalog cards' hands over purged on its own; 'most shelves stood full and the rare-book room was untouched' kills pulped and plundered.

world 2 (key pulped).reader_note: Removal by weight and the paper ministry listing two hundred tons for its printing decide pulped; plundered is the near-miss but loses to the precise reuse; the rare-book room left untouched kills purged's ideological sense and padlocked.

world 0 (key rinsed).reader_note: Clear water sinking through salt-crusted sand, then yields matching the upper slopes, means the salt was washed out: rinsed. Clear snowmelt kills replenished, bare fallow kills reseeded, standing stubble kills plowed.

world 1 (key replenished).reader_note: Dark silt over the salt crust and a gain that faded each harvest decide replenished; rinsed is the near-miss but silt covered rather than washed the crust, and 'same seed wheat' kills reseeded.

world 2 (key reseeded).reader_note: The salt crust lures rinsed, but sown yields stayed half 'as it always had' (kills rinsed and replenished) and stubble left standing kills plowed; upland water plus meadow grasses appearing on the fallow fields must be combined to get reseeded.

world 3 (key plowed).reader_note: Stubble gone, crust turned up in slabs, soil heaped into ridges with furrows, and seed sown into the furrows together describe plowing; reseeded is killed because the farmers sowed, replenished because only pale sandy soil was left; rinsed (the salt crust) is the near-miss, but the crust was broken and turned, not washed away.

world 3 (key pacemaker).reader_note: Neighbours matching within two years and traders quoting its rate make it the pacemaker; four cuts kill ratchet, the fourfold rise undercuts pendulum, regulator is a near-miss but changes followed treasury need, not market steadying.

world 0 (key ratchet).reader_note: Each change 'raised the rate' and bills to lower it 'always failed' kill pendulum and regulator; 'neighboring countries had raised their own ... years before' kills pacemaker, leaving ratchet.

world 1 (key pendulum).reader_note: 'Each undoing the one before' plus a final rate within a cent of the first decides pendulum; ratchet (one-way) is the reverse; regulator is weakened by rises coming in record-price years.

world 0 (key pooled).reader_note: Riffles dry while the bends keep depth and crowd with trout decides pooled; parched is the literal fit for the white riffles, overheated dies to shaded seepage and survival, pinched is the near-miss without the pool image.

world 1 (key pinched).reader_note: Flow down to a fifth but 'never stopped', narrow enough to step across: pinched; trout moving 'freely up and down it from bend to bend' kills pooled, nearly all alive kills overheated, and the dry white gravel margins make parched a literal near-fit.

world 2 (key overheated).reader_note: Springs holding up and canoes floating over riffles kill pinched and parched, 'ran fast and clear' kills pooled; trout dying in shallow treeless water but surviving in shade near cold springs points to heat.

world 2 (key offshoot).reader_note: Splinter party founding a temple whose head the city abbot names decides offshoot; built later kills precursor, farmhouse style kills replica, the abbot's appointment kills rival.

world 3 (key rival).reader_note: Same festival week, a gate 'carved taller', and city tolls halving point to rivalry; 'no tie to the city temple's' kills offshoot and smaller/wooden kills replica; precursor is not dated out but is weak.

world 0 (key replica).reader_note: Even the accidental chipped claw is copied at a third the size, which decides replica; offshoot is the near-miss (the families still go to the city festival); precursor is killed because a copy of a 1580 accident must come later, and rival by that dependence.

world 3 (key perch).reader_note: Birds standing along the edge between dives and leaving when the lane packs decides perch; roof literally fits the cover, fast ice that never moves kills raft, nothing growing beneath kills pantry.

world 0 (key raft).reader_note: Must combine the floes drifting south with pups nursing two weeks and arriving 'near the shoals where young seals feed' to get raft; seals climbing on to give birth make perch a strong literal fit, and 'almost nothing grows beneath them' kills pantry.

world 1 (key pantry).reader_note: Ice covering the bay literally fits roof, but the algae film feeding krill, then cod, then seals makes it a food store; raft is killed by krill staying behind when the ice drifts off, and perch is weak because seals hunt from holes rather than resting on the ice.
